effects: Sets the signer's wstETH allowance for `spender` to `amount`, replacing any earlier allowance (ERC20.approve -> _approve).
formats.shown: "Allow to spend 313.17 wstETH" with Spender address and Amount in wstETH; 2^255 and above shows as Unlimited.

findings.title: approve: interpolatedIntent leaves out the spender who gets the allowance.
findings.evidence: descriptor approve interpolatedIntent "Allow to spend {amount}"; case 0 screen "Allow to spend 313.168649898893395438 wstETH". The spender appears only as a field.

findings.title: approve: Spender addressName types allow only contracts, but any address can be a spender.
findings.evidence: descriptor approve field #.spender params.types ["contract"]; ERC20._approve only requires spender != address(0).
findings.fix: Add "eoa" and "wallet" to types, or leave types out.

cases.notes: The 313.17 wstETH approval to 0xBf67… matches the screen exactly.

effects: Lowers the signer's wstETH allowance for `spender` by `subtractedValue`. It reverts if the current allowance is smaller (ERC20.decreaseAllowance).
formats.shown: "Decrease allowance" with Spender address and Amount in wstETH. There is no sentence giving the spender or amount.

findings.title: decreaseAllowance: no interpolatedIntent, so the glance line names no token, amount or spender.
findings.evidence: descriptor decreaseAllowance has only intent "Decrease allowance"; case 4 screen has no interpolatedIntent.
findings.fix: Add interpolatedIntent "Decrease {spender} allowance by {subtractedValue}" and label the amount "Decrease by".

findings.title: decreaseAllowance: the resulting allowance depends on storage and is not shown.
findings.evidence: case 4: the Approval event sets the allowance to 0. The screen shows only the delta 0.0999998 wstETH, and the reader was unsure what remains.
findings.fix: None in the descriptor. The new allowance is current allowance minus the delta.

findings.title: decreaseAllowance: Spender types allow only contracts, but any address can be a spender.

cases.notes: The reduction by 0.0999998 wstETH for spender 0xE951… is stated. The allowance ended at 0, which the screen cannot show.

effects: Raises the signer's wstETH allowance for `spender` by `addedValue` (ERC20.increaseAllowance).
formats.shown: "Increase allowance" with Spender address and Amount in wstETH; 2^255 and above shows as Unlimited. There is no sentence.

findings.title: increaseAllowance: no interpolatedIntent, so the glance line names no token, amount or spender.
findings.evidence: descriptor increaseAllowance has only intent "Increase allowance"; case 5 screen has no interpolatedIntent.

findings.title: increaseAllowance: Spender types allow only contracts, but case 5's spender is an EOA.
findings.evidence: descriptor increaseAllowance #.spender params.types ["contract"]; case 5 spender is 0x5bDd…, which is the signer's own EOA.

cases.notes: The +100 wei increase for the signer's own address is shown. The final allowance (1000000100) depends on storage.

formats.key: permit(address owner, address spender, uint256 value, uint256 deadline, uint8 v, bytes32 r, bytes32 s)
effects: Sets `owner`'s wstETH allowance for `spender` to `value` once the owner's signature is checked; the deadline is enforced.
Uses up `owner`'s permit nonce, which makes any other pending permit signed with that nonce invalid.
Anyone can submit the call; the submitter's own tokens do not move.
formats.shown: "Permit Unlimited wstETH spending" with Owner, Spender, Amount (Unlimited above 2^255) and Deadline as a date; v, r and s are hidden.

findings.title: permit: interpolatedIntent leaves out the spender and the owner.
findings.evidence: descriptor permit interpolatedIntent "Permit {value} spending"; case 6 screen "Permit Unlimited wstETH spending".

findings.title: permit: Spender types allow only contracts, but case 6's spender is an EOA.
findings.evidence: descriptor permit #.spender params.types ["contract"]; case 6 spender 0xE66A… is the signer's EOA.

cases.notes: The signer is the spender and gains an unlimited allowance over 0x08b0…'s wstETH; Owner, Spender and Unlimited are all shown. The mined trace marks the effect signer=null.

effects: Takes `_stETHAmount` stETH from the signer to the wstETH contract through stETH.transferFrom.
Uses up `_stETHAmount` of the signer's stETH allowance to the wstETH contract.
Mints wstETH to the signer equal to stETH.getSharesByPooledEth(_stETHAmount).
formats.shown: "Wrap 0.999999999999999998 stETH" with the stETH amount field.

findings.title: wrap: the wstETH received is not shown; the contract computes it from the stETH share rate.
findings.evidence: WstETH.wrap: wstETHAmount = stETH.getSharesByPooledEth(_stETHAmount); _mint(msg.sender, wstETHAmount). Case 1: 0.813289544727858952 wstETH came in and is not on screen.
findings.fix: None in the calldata. The intent could say "into wstETH".

findings.title: wrap: the signer's stETH allowance to wstETH is used up, and the screen does not say so.
findings.evidence: WstETH.wrap: stETH.transferFrom(msg.sender, address(this), _stETHAmount). In case 1 the stETH approval to 0x7f39… went to 0. This is the prerequisite of wrapping (not_critical #12).

cases.notes: The stETH out is shown exactly. The wstETH in is implied but its amount is missing. The use of the stETH allowance is not shown.

effects: Sends the signer stETH equal to stETH.getPooledEthByShares(_wstETHAmount).
formats.shown: "Unwrap 0.000337191572414852 wstETH" with the wstETH amount; the intent says it goes to stETH.

findings.title: unwrap: the stETH received is not shown; the contract computes it from the share rate.
findings.evidence: WstETH.unwrap: stETHAmount = stETH.getPooledEthByShares(_wstETHAmount); stETH.transfer(msg.sender, stETHAmount). Case 2: 0.000414602123684846 stETH came in and is not on screen.

cases.notes: The wstETH out is shown exactly. The stETH in is named in the intent but has no amount.

effects: Moves `amount` wstETH from the signer to `recipient`.
formats.shown: "Send 0.00001 wstETH to 0xdB34…" with Recipient and Amount.

findings.title: transfer: Recipient types exclude contracts, but any non-zero address can receive.
findings.evidence: descriptor transfer #.recipient params.types ["eoa","wallet"]; ERC20._transfer only requires recipient != address(0).
findings.fix: Add "contract" to types, or leave types out.

cases.notes: The 0.00001 wstETH to 0xdB34… matches the screen.

formats.key: transferFrom(address sender, address recipient, uint256 amount)
effects: Moves `amount` wstETH from `sender` to `recipient`. These are the signer's own tokens when sender is the signer.
Lowers the signer's allowance from `sender` by `amount`, even when it is the maximum (ERC20.transferFrom calls _approve with allowance.sub(amount)).
formats.shown: "Send 0.1135 wstETH to 0x2aeD…" with Sender, Recipient and Amount.

findings.title: transferFrom: the sentence leaves out the sender, so it reads like the signer's own tokens leave.
findings.evidence: descriptor transferFrom interpolatedIntent "Send {amount} to {recipient}". In case 7 the sender is 0x08b0…, not the signer, and the reader was unsure whose tokens move.

findings.title: transferFrom: the signer's allowance from sender is spent by amount, and the screen does not say so.
findings.evidence: ERC20.transferFrom: _approve(sender, _msgSender(), _allowances[sender][_msgSender()].sub(amount)). In case 7 the allowance 0x08b0…→signer fell from max by 0.1135. Spending the allowance is what transferFrom means (#12).
findings.fix: None needed. A label such as "Uses your allowance from Sender" is optional.

findings.title: transferFrom: Sender and Recipient types exclude contracts, but both can be contracts.

cases.notes: Only the signer's allowance changed (trace marks it signer=null), and the screen does not state it. The transfer between other parties is shown correctly.
